issues.description: Field Farm.animals: the UML diagram in the problem statement declares animals: List<Animal> (problem_statement.md line 17), while the textual Part 3 of the problem statement requires using a Set implemented as a HashSet (problem_statement.md line 110). The provided solution implementation declares private List<Animal> animals (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java line 9) and initializes it as an ArrayList. This contradiction (UML -> List vs. textual spec -> Set vs. solution -> List) will confuse students about the required collection type, uniqueness semantics (no duplicates), imports, and the expected getter/setter signatures, and may cause tests or grading scripts that expect a Set/HashSet to fail.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the specification and provided code consistent. Preferred resolution: update the UML in problem_statement.md to declare animals: Set<Animal> (or animals: HashSet<Animal>) to match the textual requirement, and update the solution/template Farm.java to use java.util.Set<Animal> with an initialization animals = new HashSet<>(); change getter/setter signatures to use Set<Animal>, and ensure addAnimal, iteration (for feedAllAnimals and singFarmSong) work with Set. Alternatively, if a List is intended, remove the Set/HashSet wording from Part 3. Also update any example code/comments (Main, README) and tests to reflect the chosen collection type.
